This week, Apple has continued its steady expansion of the Apple Sports app, broadening its football coverage while also giving tennis fans a new way to follow some of the most important tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds new football leagues and tennis draws

When Apple first launched the Apple Sports app, the experience was fairly limited in terms of both the regions where it was available and the sports it actually covered.

Since then, the app has steadily evolved on both fronts — it has expanded to more than 170 countries and regions, while continually adding support for new sports, leagues and competitions.

For example, earlier this year Apple Sports rolled out to 90 new countries and introduced a slate of new features built around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports has updated once again, adding the Australian A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League and the South African Premier Division to its football line-up.

On top of that, Apple says the app can now let tennis fans "follow draw results in real time […] including draws for Grand Slams and 1000-level events", and that users can "see match-ups and results for each round at a glance".

Here are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

The football line-up continues to grow with the addition of the Australian A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League and the South African Premier Division. Tennis fans can follow draw results in real time on Apple Sports, including draws for Grand Slams and 1000-level events. See match-ups and results for each round at a glance.

Are you using Apple Sports? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
